concepts.summary: Sharpe = (R_p - R_f)/sigma_p; compare risk-adjusted, not raw return; annualize by multiplying by sqrt(periods).

concepts.concept: Limits of sigma and Sharpe: skew, fat tails, symmetry
concepts.summary: Sigma treats upside and downside alike; skewed, fat-tailed strategies (short vol) can show high Sharpe and hide crash risk.

concepts.summary: Sortino = (R - MAR)/downside deviation; penalizes only shortfalls; unstable when few observations fall below target.

concepts.summary: IR = active (excess-over-benchmark) return / tracking error; measures consistency of active skill; Sharpe uses R_f and total sigma.
concepts.lecture: 02-09 The Fundamental Law of Active Portfolio Management

sources.chapter: Ch. 9 The Fundamental Law of Active Portfolio Management
sources.note: IR = excess return per period / std of excess return; IR(alpha) = mean(alpha)/std(alpha). Book defines excess via CAPM alpha, not an explicit benchmark tracking error. (Course-assigned for a later week; not an Exam-1 reading.)

sources.chapter: Ch. 9 The Fundamental Law of Active Portfolio Management
sources.note: Return-to-risk ratio 'similar to the Sharpe ratio' but without deducting a risk-free return; called the information ratio. (Course-assigned for a later week; not an Exam-1 reading.)

sources.chapter: Grinold & Kahn, Active Portfolio Management (Information Ratio); Investopedia 'Information Ratio', 'Tracking Error', 'Sharpe Ratio'

gaps: Sortino ratio, downside deviation and MAR are only named in WHFRD (no formula). The sqrt(252) Sharpe annualization is not stated in any book (course lectures only). Tracking-error-based IR is defined via CAPM alpha in WHFRD Ch. 9 (not benchmark tracking error). Investor suitability/IPS has no book coverage. These rely on pool citations.
